subject: Going off the grid with marks

messages.author: dbc28d9e97864c4c
messages.subject: Going off the grid with marks
parts:
Hello,

I have a problem in spatial epidemiology and I was wondering if it could be solved using a log Gaussian cox process & INLA.  I have read the paper going of the grid by Simpson et al.  that implements stochastic partial differential equation approach of Lindgren et al.  and I am wondering if it can extended to handle marks? I am motivated by a paper by Liang, Carlin, and Gelfand http://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1432. They ended up tackling the big N problem another way by reducing the dimension through a predictive process. They model point patterns jointly over geographic space and nuisance covariate space, enabling the ability to show both conditional and marginal intensity associated with geographic space.

Are there any examples of using Marked lgcp's  in INLA?

Thank you for your time!
-Patrick

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Going off the grid with marks
parts:
Hi,

You can follow the 'geoestatistical under preferential sampling' example in the draft tutorial at
http://www.r-inla.org/examples/tutorials

As you have discrete marks, the problem can be simplified in a way that you can use only one Poisson likelihood with having the latent shared.

Elias
